A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete AGILE paper, including Appendices A–G. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish identical content throughout, apart from the first-page arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original jigsaw and downstream vision experiments in Tables 1–3, training-data comparisons in Figures 3–4, and training-dynamics results in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including jigsaw accuracy, nine downstream benchmark evaluations, training-data comparisons, and appendix training curves.

M1.justification: Section 3, Algorithm 1, and Appendix B retain identical swap/observe/crop/zoom interactions, cold-start training, GRPO optimization, and accuracy, format, and step rewards.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training-image sources in Appendix A, 2×2 and 3×3 jigsaw evaluation scenarios, and nine downstream vision benchmarks in Table 3.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 1–3, including GPT-4o and Gemini-2.5-Pro for jigsaws and LLaVA-OV and InternVL2.5 for downstream tasks. Figure 4 retains the same general-QA and mixed QA/jigsaw comparisons.

E3.justification: The 1.6K cold-start trajectories, 15.6K RL images, 300-image jigsaw test, Acc/Score metrics, and 20K-sample QA comparison are unchanged. Appendix D also reports identical training settings.

E4.justification: The data-scaling and QA-versus-jigsaw analyses in Figures 3–4, case studies in Figures 5 and 7–10, and training-dynamics analysis in Appendix E are identical.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged across the tables and plots, including Figure 11. No repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are newly disclosed.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results match. Both report final RL accuracies of 82.8% for 2×2 and 20.8% for 3×3 jigsaws in Table 1, and a downstream average of 65.2 in Table 3. Analysis plots and appendix trajectories are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The jigsaw-state definitions in Equations 1–3, GRPO objective in Equation 4, and reward formulations in Equations 5–6 are identical. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about interactive jigsaw learning, improved perception and reasoning, downstream generalization, and scalable multimodal RL data.

C2.justification: The interpretations of data scaling, proxy-task transfer, and training dynamics are unchanged. Appendix F retains the computational-overhead and context-window limitations that restrict RL training to 2×2 puzzles.

D1.justification: Implementation frameworks, eight 80GB A100 GPUs, Appendix B prompts, and Tables 4–5 hyperparameters are identical. The repository link and stated code/data release information also remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list are identical, including positioning relative to Jigsaw-R1 and other reinforcement-learning and proxy-task approaches. No cited works or novelty comparisons change.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1, 1 Oct 2025, to v2, 10 Feb 2026. This is a metadata-only text update; wording, author information, headings, and main-text and appendix organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: All eleven figures, five tables, and Algorithm 1 retain identical content, formatting, captions, and placement. The version/date stamp update does not alter the document's substantive layout.

improvement.justification: v2 preserves the scientific content, experimental evidence, reproducibility information, limitations, and substantive presentation of v1, including all appendices. Updating only the arXiv version/date stamp provides no meaningful improvement or deterioration in paper quality.
